reason: README Usage snippet quantizes a small PyTorch model with coreai_opt on CPU, no gated resources.
demo: README 'Getting started > Usage' INT8 weight-only quantization snippet
goal: Install coreai-opt (pip install coreai-opt or from source, Python>=3.11, CPU torch) and run the README Usage snippet: build the small Sequential model, Quantizer(model, QuantizerConfig.presets.w8()), prepare(example_inputs) and finalize(). It must run without errors and the prepared model must give a finite (1,10) output close to the original model's.
check: A script runs the README quantization flow on a small model and verifies finalize succeeds and the quantized model's output is finite, correctly shaped and close to the float output.

revision.by: fairness review (every maintained-set exam re-checked against the source)
issues: Too lenient: it only checks that the prepared model's output is within 0.2 of the float output, which a no-op quantizer would also pass. The finalized model (the README's 'Finalize for Core AI export' result) is never run

v2 runs the finalized model, as the repo's own preset test does. It checks shape, finiteness and a small error against float (<0.05), and requires a non-zero difference so the INT8 weights must actually take effect
Drops `python -I`, which would ignore a PYTHONPATH-based from-source setup that the goal allows; no shadowing risk because the package is in src/
evidence: src/coreai_opt/quantization/quantizer.py:526-533 - finalize replaces fake quantization with Core AI quantized ops
src/coreai_opt/quantization/_graph/_prepare_for_export.py:729-790 - weights replaced by pre-quantized constexpr_blockwise_shift_scale ops
data/runs/apple-coreai-optimization/deliverables/NOTES.md - prepared output differs from float by ~1.8e-3
